name: i18n-live-locale-switch
description: Regression test for issue #457 Bug 1: switching locale while a panel is already open must re-render that panel's static text (title, buttons, toolbar captions) in place, without the panel being closed and reopened. Also verifies a fired event renders fully in French when the locale is already French. Extended for issue #492 section 3: after the locale switch, opens the tutorial and the Crew panel together (panels open, tutorial up) and asserts the tutorial coach card's CLOCK HELD tooltip/chip and EventModal's CLOCK HELD chip — both built with a raw t() call at construction time, before the switch happens — read French, not the English baked in at app boot; also asserts the Settings panel's active-language pill matches the current locale. Locale is switched once, before tutorial_start rather than literally mid-step, because the tutorial's own rails (src/ui/tutorialGuide.ts) make every button except the current step's target inert — including the Settings toggle — so a real player cannot open Settings once the coach card is up; EventModal is exempt from that gate (it's a `.bs-confirm-overlay` modal), which is why its own CLOCK HELD chip is checked with an event fired while the tutorial card is not yet started.

steps.description: Open the Settings panel via the toolbar — English baseline, panel now open.
Click FR inside the still-open Settings panel WITHOUT closing it. Core Bug 1 regression: title, English/French buttons, Close button, and toolbar captions must switch to French in place.

expect.note: the panel itself must still be usable (not torn down/rebuilt broken) after switching locale in place — the actual French text is verified visually via screenshot, not state, since expect has no text-content field

steps.description: Open the Build menu (Settings auto-hides via the toolbar's mutual-exclusion) — panel opened fresh while locale is already French, confirming the switch persists beyond the panel that triggered it.

expect.note: toolbar panels are mutually exclusive — opening Build must hide Settings

steps.description: Fire an event while locale is French — dialog title/description/option labels must render in French, not English. — `event fire` is a test hook with no UI and none intended. Left unmarked.

Resolve the event through its own buttons, then open the top-bar Save/Load panel (opened via main.ts, outside UIManager) while the locale is French -- checks whether that panel picked up the live-switch fix too. Hard clicks, not clickIfPresent: the preceding step fires this event explicitly, so the dialog is guaranteed. The trailing #bs-saveload-btn click is what opens the saves modal the NEXT step asserts against -- a blanket conversion replaced this whole interaction array and silently dropped it, which is what broke this file.

Close the Save/Load modal opened above via its own close button before continuing — its .bs-confirm-overlay backdrop otherwise stays on top of the page and blocks every later click (toolbar/Settings recheck, tutorial start), the same class of gap documented in rock-fragmenter-breaking.json for the Blast Report modal. SavesModal's header is a plain div (not a <header> element), and its close button is the only button in the modal without a data-action attribute (slot buttons all carry save-here/load/delete) — :not([data-action]) is what actually isolates it.

Issue #492 section 3 extension: pause so a fired event's CLOCK HELD chip is visible, then fire the tutorial consultant event (its 3 options carry no risky/probabilistic hints, so its only bsx-chip-warn is the CLOCK HELD chip itself — see TutorialEvents.ts). EventModal.clockChip is built with a raw t() call at construction and never registered with the panel's own LocaleTextRegistry (bug 3 of #492 section 3): this must read the French translation, not the English text baked in when the app booted.
CLOCK HELD chip must read the French translation of ui.event.clock_held ('HORLOGE ARRÊTÉE'), not the English text EventModal's constructor baked in at app boot.

Answered through the event dialog's own buttons. A HARD click, not clickIfPresent: the preceding step fires this event explicitly (event fire), so the dialog is guaranteed on screen and a permissive click would be too weak -- if it silently found nothing, the dialog would stay up and cover the next step's target, which is exactly how this file broke when a blanket conversion treated every event choose as a random roll.
Reopen Settings and confirm the active-language pill matches the current locale (French) — syncLangPills toggles the `active` class onto whichever pill matches the live locale.

Start the tutorial while locale is already French. TutorialOverlay is constructed once at app boot (always in English, before the player can switch locale) — its coach card must not still be showing the English text baked in at construction. Bug 1 of #492 section 3: pausedEl.title and pausedChipEl.textContent are only ever set at construction, never re-applied by TutorialOverlay.refreshLocale() (a no-op stub) or reached by main.ts's language-change fan-out.

interaction.expectedValue: Le temps est en pause jusqu'à cette action — le tutoriel retient l'horloge pour que le site ne prenne pas d'avance sur vous.

expect.note: tutorial rails (src/ui/tutorialGuide.ts) make every control but the current step's own target inert, including the Settings toggle -- confirms a player cannot switch language again once the tutorial has engaged, matching the deleted playtest's tutorial-fr.json beat 2 (checked there before tutorial_start; checked here after, on the toggle itself rather than the panel it opens).

steps.description: Advance past the time-speed step (its own target, always reachable) so the Crew panel — the hire-surveyor step's rails target — becomes clickable, proving a panel can be opened mid-tutorial while the locale switch made earlier is still in effect.

Open the Crew panel — a second panel, open at the same time as the tutorial card. CrewPanel's title is already registered with its own LocaleTextRegistry (unlike EventModal's clockChip), so this is a locked-in green check confirming a second panel keeps reading French while the tutorial overlay is up alongside it, not just the panel that made the switch.
